"India's reforms of 1991 aimed at greater integration with the world economy. Resistance to globalisation in India has come from left-wing groups, trade unions and farmers. The Indian Social Forum also raised voices against neo-liberal globalisation."
(i) India embarked on a programme of economic reforms in: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'World Social Forum' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The World Social Forum became an important platform against neo-liberal globalisation. (2)
items.answer: (i) 1991 (ii) An open meeting place of human rights activists, environmentalists, labour, youth and women opposed to neo-liberal globalisation. (iii) It brought together activists, environmentalists, labour, youth and women from many countries.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) 1991 (ii) An open meeting place of human rights activists, environmentalists, labour, youth and women opposed to neo-liberal globalisation. (iii) It brought together activists, environmentalists, labour, youth and women from many countries.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Technology is the most important cause of globalisation.
Reason (R): Inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made communication and flows across the world fast and cheap.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made communication and flows across the world fast and cheap.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about India and resistance to globalisation is NOT correct?
items.answer: India has always followed an open economic policy.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. India was protectionist before 1991.
options: India has always followed an open economic policy.
Resistance to globalisation in India has come from left-wing groups, trade unions and farmers.
The Indian Social Forum also raised voices against neo-liberal globalisation.
Resistance to globalisation is not anti-globalisation in every case; some movements seek a different kind of globalisation.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? The process in which outside influences enrich and combine with local cultures, making each culture more distinctive.
items.answer: cultural heterogenisation
items.markingKey: (a) cultural heterogenisation: the process in which outside influences enrich and combine with local cultures, making each culture more distinctive.
options: cultural heterogenisation
globalisation
World Social Forum
new economic policy

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Economic globalisation has uneven effects.
Reason (R): It has benefited some sections of society and countries more than others.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: it has benefited some sections of society and countries more than others.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the concept and causes of globalisation:
I. The ability of ideas, capital, commodities and people to move more easily from one part of the world to another has been made possible by technology.
II. Globalisation has a long history, but its scale and speed in the contemporary era are unprecedented.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Assertion (A): India has always followed an open economic policy.
Reason (R): Before 1991 India followed a protectionist policy, restricting imports and foreign investment.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: India was protectionist before 1991. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by 'technology' in the context of the concept and causes of globalisation?
items.answer: The major cause of globalisation, as inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made flows faster.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: technology correctly explained as the major cause of globalisation, as inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made flows faster.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the concept and causes of globalisation and answer the questions that follow.
"The flows involved in globalisation include ideas, capital, commodities and people. Globalisation has a long history, but its scale and speed in the contemporary era are unprecedented. The ability of ideas, capital, commodities and people to move more easily from one part of the world to another has been made possible by technology."
(i) Which of the following is an example of a flow in globalisation? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'technology' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Technology is the most important cause of globalisation. (2)
items.answer: (i) Movement of capital from one country to another (ii) The major cause of globalisation, as inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made flows faster. (iii) Inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made communication and flows across the world fast and cheap.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Movement of capital from one country to another (ii) The major cause of globalisation, as inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made flows faster. (iii) Inventions like the telegraph, telephone, microchip and internet made communication and flows across the world fast and cheap.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the consequences of globalisation:
I. Economic globalisation involves greater trade, foreign investment and the movement of capital across countries.
II. Globalisation has led to differing views – some see it as benefiting the few, others as increasing prosperity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the consequences of globalisation:
I. Globalisation has led to differing views – some see it as benefiting the few, others as increasing prosperity.
II. Economic globalisation involves greater trade, foreign investment and the movement of capital across countries.
III. Cultural globalisation can also make us more open and enlarge our choices.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (d) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.
options: III only
I only
I and III only
All of them

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about India and resistance to globalisation:
I. Only left-wing groups have opposed globalisation in India.
II. India's reforms of 1991 aimed at greater integration with the world economy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: II only
items.markingKey: (b) I is incorrect: Right-wing groups have also objected, mainly to foreign cultural influences. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem: "Events in one part of the world affect other parts." Examine this statement with reference to the concept and causes of globalisation.
items.answer: The statement is valid. Globalisation has created worldwide interconnectedness.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (globalisation has created worldwide interconnectedness.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about the consequences of globalisation is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Cultural globalisation always destroys local cultures."
items.answer: It can also produce heterogenisation, enriching local cultures.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (It can also produce heterogenisation, enriching local cultures.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the consequences of globalisation is correct?
items.answer: Globalisation has led to differing views – some see it as benefiting the few, others as increasing prosperity.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Developed countries restrict the movement of people through visas. It can also produce heterogenisation, enriching local cultures. The state remains important; its capacity has changed but not disappeared.
options: Under globalisation people move as freely as capital.
Globalisation has led to differing views – some see it as benefiting the few, others as increasing prosperity.
Globalisation has completely ended the role of the state.
Cultural globalisation always destroys local cultures.

items.stem: In the study of India and resistance to globalisation, the term 'new economic policy' refers to:
items.answer: The policy of economic reforms launched in India in 1991, opening the economy to trade and investment
items.markingKey: (c) 'new economic policy' means the policy of economic reforms launched in India in 1991, opening the economy to trade and investment.
options: Flows of ideas, capital, commodities and people across different parts of the world, creating worldwide interconnectedness
A state that performs only core functions such as maintaining law and order and security, leaving economic and social matters to the market
The policy of economic reforms launched in India in 1991, opening the economy to trade and investment
A state that provides social security and welfare to its citizens, said to be giving way to a minimalist state under globalisation

items.stem: The following statement about the concept and causes of globalisation is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Technology has played no role in globalisation."
items.answer: Technology has been a critical cause, enabling fast flows.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Technology has been a critical cause, enabling fast flows.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the consequences of globalisation and answer the questions that follow.
"Globalisation has led to an erosion of state capacity in some respects, as markets become important determinants of economic and social priorities. In some respects state capacity has increased, as states have access to new technology to collect information about citizens. Cultural globalisation can also make us more open and enlarge our choices."
(i) Economic globalisation is driven by institutions such as the: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'minimalist state' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Critics fear cultural homogenisation. (2)
items.answer: (i) IMF and WTO (ii) A state that performs only core functions such as maintaining law and order and security, leaving economic and social matters to the market. (iii) The culture of the economically and politically dominant societies, especially the US, spreads around the world.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) IMF and WTO (ii) A state that performs only core functions such as maintaining law and order and security, leaving economic and social matters to the market. (iii) The culture of the economically and politically dominant societies, especially the US, spreads around the world.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: Trade unions and farmers in India have protested against aspects of globalisation.
items.answer: They fear job losses, entry of multinational companies and threats to livelihoods.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: They fear job losses, entry of multinational companies and threats to livelihoods. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem:
Statement: Economic globalisation has uneven effects.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: It has benefited some sections of society and countries more than others.
items.markingKey: (a) It has benefited some sections of society and countries more than others.
options: It has benefited some sections of society and countries more than others.
Globalisation has created worldwide interconnectedness.
The welfare state is giving way to a minimalist state and markets determine economic priorities.
The culture of the economically and politically dominant societies, especially the US, spreads around the world.
